To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we give a new general reduction from deletion against adaptive sequences to non-adaptive sequences; (b) we show in theory that prior work for non-adaptive sequences fails against adaptive sequences, and (c) we design a practical attack on a popular algorithm for adaptive deletion.

(1) we give a general method for obtaining provable deletion guarantees even for deletion sequences that are chosen adaptively to the published models; and (2) we show in practice how prior work fails against such adaptive sequences, and give an attack on SISA, which was previously thought to be secure against adaptive deletions.

1) prior work on deletion algorithms for non-convext models does not work against adaptive deletion sequences; 2) we give a reduction from guarantees for adaptive sequences to guarantees for non-adapative sequences; 3) this reduction gives strong guarantees in practice against adaptive deletion sequences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: how do we design algorithms which are provably secure against deletion by users who can adapt their deletions to published models?
the question of how we should delete data from trained machine learning models, given that we don’t know the future deletion sequences.
